extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation across nine domains (e.g., games, SVG, web applications, simulations). It features an automated, multimodal evaluation pipeline that renders artifacts, captures three-step temporal screenshots, and scores outputs using a fine-grained, per-task checklist with an MLLM-as-Judge. Tasks are stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers to support fine-grained capability analysis.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles with human verification. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist generated by LLM and human-refined. A 10% manually curated seed was used for calibration. Solvability was validated by collecting candidate solutions from multiple model families.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Software Collection; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and screenshots used as input for LLM visual-to-query generation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities, LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. For human validation, 280 queries with outputs from 6 models were independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience under a double-blind protocol; samples appeared in randomized order and the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 was achieved among annotators on the manually curated seed set. For the human validation study, pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was computed: for each query with m model responses, m(m−1)/2 unique pairs were formed and the number of concordant pairs between the MLLM referee and human judges was counted; the consistency rate is the ratio of concordant pairs to total pairs. The final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos (checklist generation); Gemini-2.5-Pro (query classification, checklist generation, automated scoring referee); LLMs used for prompt rewriting and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots; MinHash and semantic similarity tools for de-duplication; screenshot perceptual hashing; lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Minor discrepancies are observed in the fine-grained scoring of certain complex interactive tasks, reflecting potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Discrete screenshot sampling may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions; the benchmark evaluates only the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities; distillation on limited data may be insufficient for robust generalization
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench is intended to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models by providing a scalable and accurate evaluation tool; the authors note that high-fidelity, functional interactive visual artifacts are central to user experience in modern applications and that their quality directly affects real-world adoption.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The quality filtering prompt explicitly screens for privacy by checking whether queries avoid requesting or involving any sensitive personal information, such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate high-quality interactive visual artifacts from multimodal instructions; benchmarking and comparing LLM code generation capabilities across visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality; providing fine-grained diagnostics to guide development of user-centric generative models
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released; future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks solved only by brittle hacks (e.g., hard-coded coordinates that break under minor viewport changes) were revised or removed. Difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard) were assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs to enforce a 30%/40%/30% split. Prompt rewriting added diverse styles via LLM rewriting. A 10% manually curated seed was used as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control was applied: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability, and humans verified. Underspecified items identified during solvability validation were pruned or revised.
